result:
The flow is **body text → resolved `UserId`s → saved comment and `comment.created` event → notification rows → inbox rendering**. The email part has a gap: selecting the `"email"` channel does not trigger an immediate mention email in this implementation.

The issue page, `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/projects/[projectSlug]/issues/[issueNumber]/page.tsx`, loads up to 100 organization members and passes them to `CommentComposer`, with `createCommentAction` as its submit handler. In `src/components/domain/comment/mention-textarea.tsx`, `MentionTextarea.handleInput()` calls `emit()`, which runs `resolveMentions(body, members)` from `src/lib/mentions.ts` on every change. Autocomplete uses `findMentionQuery()`, `matchMembers()`, and `applyMention()` in `src/components/domain/comment/mention-query.ts`; accepting a suggestion inserts the member’s email handle into the body.

`src/lib/mentions.ts` performs the actual text-to-user mapping. `extractMentions()` strips fenced code blocks and inline code, extracts recognized `@handle` tokens, lowercases them, and removes duplicates. `handleOf()` defines a member’s handle as the lowercase part of their email before `@`. `resolveMentions()` maps those handles to `MemberWithUser.userId`, drops unknown handles, and deduplicates the resulting IDs. Thus `@someone` resolves through an organization member’s email handle, rather than their display name.

`CommentComposer` in `src/components/domain/comment/comment-composer.tsx` keeps that list in its `mentioned` state. Its `handleSubmit()` validates and submits it as `CreateCommentInput.mentionedUserIds`, alongside the body, organization, and issue. `createCommentSchema` in `src/schemas/comment.ts` defaults the list to `[]` and permits at most 50 submitted IDs. On the server, `createCommentAction()` in `src/actions/comments/create-comment.ts` uses `withAction()` from `src/actions/_lib/with-action.ts` to revalidate the input and authenticate the actor, then checks permission and rate limits before calling `createComment()`.

`createComment()` in `src/server/services/comment-service.ts` checks organization scope, issue permission, archive state, and its rate limit. It then calls its private `resolveMentionedUsers()`: this loads the first 100 nonarchived organization members through `listMembers()` in `src/server/repositories/member-repository.ts`, resolves the body again, and returns the deduplicated **union of server-resolved IDs and client-provided IDs found in that member list**. Client IDs can therefore survive even without a matching token in the body. `insertComment()` in `src/server/repositories/comment-repository.ts` saves the resulting list as JSON in `mentioned_user_ids`. Only after insertion does the service await `emit("comment.created", …)`, carrying the same `mentionedUserIds`, plus the comment ID, issue ID, organization, actor, and timestamp. That payload is defined by `TaskflowEventMap["comment.created"]` in `src/types/event.ts`.

The notification subscriber is installed ahead of requests: `register()` in `src/instrumentation.ts` imports `src/server/services/event-registry.ts`, whose import of `notification-service.ts` runs `registerFanOut()`. Its `comment.created` handler first calls `notify()` for the issue author and assignee with kind `"comment_created"`, then calls it for `payload.mentionedUserIds` with kind `"comment_mention"`. It consumes the supplied IDs without reparsing the body. A mentioned author or assignee can receive both kinds. `emit()` in `src/lib/event-bus.ts` waits for subscribers to settle but isolates their failures, so a saved comment does not guarantee successful notification insertion.

`notify()` in `src/server/services/notification-service.ts` deduplicates recipients, skips the actor themselves, and loads each recipient’s **organization/user/kind-specific** preference using `getPreference()` in `src/server/repositories/notification-preference-repository.ts`. Its `resolveChannels()` makes the selection:

- No preference row selects `["in_app", "email"]`.
- An explicit preference selects `"in_app"` when `inApp` is true.
- It selects `"email"` when `email && (!digestOnly || isEnabled("digest_email", flags))`.
- An empty selection skips the recipient entirely.

The digest flag uses the organization’s plan and overrides; `src/config/feature-flags.ts` enables it for Growth and higher, or an allowed override, evaluated by `isEnabled()` in `src/lib/feature-flags.ts`. Ordinary email selection bypasses that flag. `updateNotificationPreferenceAction()` in `src/actions/notifications/update-preferences.ts` also rejects enabling `digestOnly` while the flag is unavailable.

For every nonempty selection, `insertNotifications()` in `src/server/repositories/notification-repository.ts` writes **one database row**, with JSON `channels`, `readAt: null`, and the mention title/body/issue link. The inbox `Page()` in `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/inbox/page.tsx` calls the service’s `listNotifications()`, which checks scope and permission and delegates to the repository. `NotificationList` in `src/components/domain/notification/notification-list.tsx` renders those rows, ordering unread ones first. **Neither the query nor the renderer filters by `"in_app"`**, so even an email-only selection currently appears in the inbox.

Finally, `notify()` never calls an email renderer or sender. Although `src/emails/mention-email.tsx` defines `MentionEmail` and `src/emails/render.ts` supports it through `renderTemplate()`, that template is not wired into this flow. A later digest can include the row: `runDigestEmailJob()` in `src/server/jobs/digest-email-job.ts` checks the organization’s digest hour and flag, gets users with any `digestOnly` preference, and calls `buildDigest()` in `src/server/services/digest-service.ts`. The digest collects unread rows in its time window **without filtering their channels or individual kind preferences**, renders them, calls `sendEmail()`, and marks included rows read. `sendEmail()` in `src/server/services/email-service.ts` only logs `email.sent`; it has no outbound transport.

Consequently, the current code creates an inbox row whenever any channel survives, creates no mention row for self-mentions, unresolved handles, or an empty channel selection, and sends no immediate mention email. Eligible rows may later contribute to a logged digest.
